name: AI Agent Engineering
tagline: Build LLM-powered agents that use tools, memory and planning to finish real work.

overview.summary: AI agent engineers build software where a large language model (LLM) does more than chat: it decides which tools to call (APIs, databases, browsers, code), keeps memory between steps, and works toward a goal with checks and human approval where needed. Think of it as backend engineering where one of the components is a reasoning model, and your job is to make it reliable, safe, observable and cheap enough to run in production.
whyTrending: LinkedIn's Jobs on the Rise 2026 list ranked AI engineer as the fastest-growing role, and companies are moving from chatbots to agents that complete multi-step tasks.

Open standards like the Model Context Protocol (MCP) made it easy to connect models to tools and data; MCP is now supported across major model providers and was placed under the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation in late 2025.

Every major cloud and model vendor now ships an agent SDK (OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, Claude Agent SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework), so demand has spread beyond AI labs to banks, hospitals, SaaS and consulting firms.
Employers need engineers who can evaluate, secure and monitor agents — skills that most developers have not yet learned, which keeps the talent gap wide.

roles.title: AI Agent Engineer
roles.description: Designs and ships agent workflows: tool definitions, planning loops, memory, guardrails and human-in-the-loop approval steps.

roles.title: AI / LLM Application Engineer
roles.description: Integrates LLMs into products with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), structured outputs and streaming UIs.

roles.title: Agent Platform Engineer
roles.description: Builds the internal platform agents run on: MCP servers, sandboxes, auth, rate limiting, cost tracking and observability.

roles.title: AI Evaluation Engineer
roles.description: Creates test sets, automated graders and regression suites so teams can measure agent quality before and after each change.

roles.title: Forward-Deployed / Solutions Engineer (AI)
roles.description: Works directly with customers to design and deploy agents for their workflows, then feeds lessons back to the product team.

roles.title: Conversational AI Developer
roles.description: Builds voice and chat agents for support, sales and operations, connecting them to CRMs, ticketing and telephony.

beginner: Python fundamentals (functions, classes, async basics, virtual environments)
Calling an LLM API and handling JSON responses
Prompt basics: system prompts, few-shot examples, structured output
REST APIs and HTTP with requests/httpx
Reading API documentation and rate-limit/cost basics
intermediate: Tool / function calling and schema design
Agent frameworks such as LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK or Claude Agent SDK
Evaluation: golden datasets, LLM-as-judge, regression tests
Observability with tracing tools (LangSmith, Langfuse, OpenTelemetry)
TypeScript for agent UIs and Node-based tooling
advanced: Multi-agent orchestration and long-running, durable workflows
Agent security: prompt injection defence, sandboxing, least-privilege tool access
Cost and latency optimisation (caching, model routing, batching)
Fine-tuning or distilling small models for specific agent tasks
Designing human-in-the-loop review and audit trails
Production deployment with containers, queues and autoscaling

stack.note: Job listings most often pair Python with at least one agent framework and one vector database. TypeScript shows up whenever the role touches product UI or Node-based MCP servers.

roadmap.title: LLM foundations
goals: Get comfortable with Python, virtual environments and async/await
Call two different LLM APIs and compare outputs, latency and cost
Practise structured outputs (JSON schema) and basic prompt patterns
Build a simple RAG Q&A bot over your own notes or PDFs
Learn what tokens, context windows and temperature mean in practice
roadmap.milestone: A deployed RAG chatbot with a README that explains its design and limits.

roadmap.title: Tools, agents & MCP
goals: Implement function calling from scratch without a framework
Rebuild the same agent with LangGraph or an official agent SDK
Write your own MCP server that exposes 2–3 tools (e.g. calendar, database, files)
Add memory: short-term conversation state and long-term vector memory
Add tracing so you can see every model call and tool call
roadmap.milestone: A tool-using agent that completes a 3+ step task end to end, with traces you can show.

roadmap.title: Production quality
goals: Create an evaluation set of 30–50 test cases and an automated scorer
Defend against prompt injection and restrict tool permissions
Add a human approval step for risky actions
Containerise the agent and deploy it with logging and cost tracking
Write a case study: problem, architecture, eval results, trade-offs
roadmap.milestone: A portfolio-grade agent with evals, guardrails and a written case study — ready for interviews.

interview.question: What is the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent?
interview.answer: A chatbot replies to messages. An agent pursues a goal: it plans, calls tools, observes results and loops until the task is done or it needs a human, so it can take actions, not just produce text.

interview.question: How does function/tool calling work?
interview.answer: You describe tools with names and JSON schemas. The model returns a structured request to call a tool with arguments; your code runs it, sends the result back, and the model continues with that new information.

interview.question: What is RAG and when would you use it instead of fine-tuning?
interview.answer: Retrieval-augmented generation fetches relevant documents at query time and adds them to the prompt. Use it when knowledge changes often or must be cited; fine-tune when you need a consistent style or behaviour, not fresh facts.

interview.question: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
interview.answer: An open protocol that standardises how AI applications connect to tools and data. A server exposes tools, resources and prompts; any MCP-compatible client can use them without custom integration code.

interview.question: How do you evaluate an agent?
interview.answer: Build a dataset of realistic tasks with expected outcomes, score final results and intermediate steps (right tool, right arguments), use code checks where possible and LLM-as-judge where needed, and run it on every change to catch regressions.

interview.question: What is prompt injection and how do you defend against it?
interview.answer: Malicious instructions hidden in user input or retrieved content that try to hijack the agent. Defences include treating external content as data, least-privilege tools, allow-lists, output validation and human approval for sensitive actions.

interview.question: How would you reduce the cost of an agent in production?
interview.answer: Route easy steps to smaller models, cache prompts and results, trim context, cap loop iterations, batch requests where possible and monitor cost per task with tracing.

interview.question: When should you use multiple agents instead of one?
interview.answer: Only when tasks are truly separable or need different tools/permissions. Multi-agent systems add latency, cost and failure points, so start with one well-designed agent and split only when evals show a benefit.

interview.question: How do you handle agent memory?
interview.answer: Short-term memory is the conversation/state passed each step; long-term memory is stored externally (database or vector store) and retrieved when relevant. Summarise old context to stay within the context window.

interview.question: What would you log for an agent in production?
interview.answer: Every model call (input, output, tokens, latency, model version), every tool call with arguments and results, errors, user feedback and final outcome — with sensitive data redacted.

demandNotes.bangladesh: Early but growing: software firms serving foreign clients and local fintech/telecom teams are adding LLM features. Few postings say 'agent engineer' yet — look for 'AI engineer', 'LLM engineer' or 'Python + LLM'.
demandNotes.remote: Very high. Startups worldwide hire remote AI engineers who can show working agents and evals; a public portfolio matters more than a degree.
demandNotes.global: Very high. AI engineer tops LinkedIn's 2026 fastest-growing jobs list, and the WEF expects AI/ML specialists to be among the fastest-growing roles to 2030.
